headline: Settlement gain lifts profit while tariffs squeeze margins
summary_short: Gap's net sales rose 1% y/y to $3,497M as comp sales grew 2%, but gross margin fell to 40.5% on tariff costs; net income jumped 76% to $339M, largely reflecting a $313M credit-card settlement gain net of a $50M charitable contribution.
summary_long: Net sales rose 1% y/y to $3,497M on 2% comp growth (Gap Global +10%, Athleta -11%). Gross margin fell 130bp to 40.5% as tariffs added ~2 points to cost of goods, partly offset by less Gap Global promotion. Operating income jumped to $445M from $260M, mainly reflecting a $313M interchange-fee litigation settlement net of a $50M charitable contribution. Net income rose to $339M; diluted EPS $0.90. Free cash flow improved to $78M from -$223M on the settlement cash and lower inventory build; the company repurchased $361M of stock and paid a $0.175/share dividend. No forward guidance was included in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Results were lifted by a one-time $313M credit-card interchange-fee litigation settlement net of a $50M concurrent charitable contribution; underlying trends were positive comp sales offset by tariff-driven gross-margin compression.
Net sales rose 1% y/y, driven by an increase across all brands except Athleta Global, consistent with the 2% consolidated comp-sales gain (Gap Global +10%, Old Navy +1%, Athleta -11%).

Cost of goods sold rose about 1.0 point of sales on an estimated ~2-point tariff impact net of mitigation, partly offset by less Gap Global promotion; occupancy costs rose 0.3 points on store population.
Operating expenses fell as a % of sales mainly due to the $313M interchange-fee settlement gain, partly offset by the $50M charitable contribution and an increase in strategic investments.
Shard EBIT ($472M) exceeds reported operating income ($445M) by $27M; the increase tracks the same settlement gain cited for operating income, not a separately disclosed cause.
EBITDA move reflects the same $313M settlement gain plus $128M of depreciation and amortization added back; not framed as a distinct driver in the filing.
Net income rose on the settlement gain flowing through operating income, plus a lower effective tax rate (24.7% vs 26.6%) from favorable share-based compensation and foreign entity tax benefits.
EPS gain reflects higher net income plus a lower weighted-average basic share count (367M vs 375M) from ongoing buybacks.
Diluted EPS rose in step with basic EPS; the diluted share count (378M vs 382M) also fell y/y, partly due to anti-dilutive stock-unit and unsettled ASR-share exclusions.
